html:
Controller inference lifecycle and model bindings

The optional Inference subsystem manages model-serving processes. The Controller coordinates changes to those processes with accepted Agent work. Starting an inference operation returns an acceptance record; readiness, model compatibility and cleanup have their own later outcomes.

This guide explains the Controller boundary in InferenceManager, its tool adapter, route contracts and application integration. The shared inference architecture owns Portal planning, distributed workers, resource reservations, installation and diagnostics. Use the Inference manual for operator workflows. The observation guide follows serving status, request/GPU captures, renewal and exports separately from process lifecycle. The shared Portal launch guide follows planning, member reservations, distributed workers, readiness and cleanup beneath this boundary.

Owners and data paths

The application installs the manager only when the compiled feature allows inference. Its state lives in inference/ beside the current-run database. Portal uses its own revisioned SQLite records and private secret storage; it is an explicit external store outside the Controller's core RAM domains.

flowchart TD U[Authenticated management UI] --> H[Managed HTTP routes] A[Agent inference tools] --> T[Route-derived typed contracts] H --> G[Shared actor and mutation guard] T --> G G --> P[Portal management operations] G --> M[Controller lifecycle manager] M --> O[Durable operation intents and admission holds] M --> P P --> S[Supervisor and local or remote workers] P --> L[Published launch generations] B[Versioned model bindings] --> C[Managed client resolution] L --> C O --> N[Native model admission] C --> N N --> I[Ordinary model requests]

HTTP writes require the enclosing Controller login/CSRF boundary and reject cross-origin requests. Integrated routes reject direct local worker-protocol calls; remote worker protocol remains with standalone hosts. Tool schemas are derived from the same route signatures, excluding internal operations. Tool writes still pass through normal execution permissions.

The shared guard serializes ordinary mutations, checks management phase and requires current revisions for existing editable records. Stop, force-stop and duplicate actions bypass that mutation lock so a slow inspection cannot hold them behind it. Server-update admission remains a separate gate. Read-only operations receive actor context without taking the mutation lock. Validation only plans; duplication saves a separate profile. Neither becomes a lifecycle launch intent.

Agent intent and receipt ordering

An Agent may request a change to the model server that is serving its own request. The manager therefore stores its lifecycle intent as awaiting_receipt. Only a matching successful native invocation receipt releases that intent for execution. Reading an operation record does not release it.

sequenceDiagram participant L as Native tool owner participant T as Inference adapter participant M as Inference manager participant P as Portal records participant S as Native receipt store L->>T: Invoke lifecycle tool with run and operation IDs T->>M: Validate and invoke on manager event loop M->>P: Save intent as awaiting_receipt P-->>M: Stable lifecycle operation ID M-->>T: Accepted intent T-->>L: Success receipt with matching private intent metadata L->>S: Commit claimed invocation receipt L->>M: after_receipt for the newly accepted call M->>M: Schedule one lifecycle worker Note over M,P: Acceptance precedes process changes

The callback is wired through operation metadata and the outer claimed-call owner. Reused receipts do not fire it again. Native-store acceptance follows the Controller persistence boundary; this ordering does not wait for a checkpoint to flush. The adapter waits at most 330 seconds for a response; a timeout reports an unknown effect because the submitted management work can continue.

User lifecycle actions queue immediately. Matching idempotency keys reuse the operation when action, instance and Agent run identity match; a conflicting fingerprint fails. Concurrent equivalent lifecycle actions can share an existing operation even without a key. A user can take over a matching deferred Agent intent. Stop, force-stop, delete and subsystem shutdown can preempt conflicting work.

Instance transitions and admission

An admission hold is a set of normalized model endpoint identities. The manager persists those holds, publishes their union and wakes native admission waiters when the set changes. If a restart publishes a different address, both old and new addresses remain held until the transition is verified.

sequenceDiagram participant M as Lifecycle worker participant R as Native admission and checkpoint owner participant P as Portal and Supervisor participant S as Operation records alt Force-stop M->>R: Hold endpoints and record affected work M->>P: Force worker cleanup before predecessor wait P-->>M: Worker cleanup completed M->>R: Release active calls on held addresses M->>M: Join superseded lifecycle cleanup else Ordinary transition M->>M: Join superseded lifecycle cleanup M->>R: Hold endpoints and record affected work M->>R: Request background checkpoint without waiting opt Stop, restart or delete M->>P: Stop owned instance P-->>M: Worker cleanup completed M->>R: Release active calls on held addresses end end opt Start or restart M->>P: Start captured candidate profile M->>P: Wait for ready state within readiness budget M->>M: Verify current and accepted-task model bindings M->>R: Release transition hold and wake waiters end M->>S: Record completed operation Note over M,R: No wait for active requests or checkpoint disk I/O

Force-stop skips the checkpoint request. Ordinary transitions request a checkpoint but do not wait for disk I/O or active model calls. Verified worker cleanup allows the manager to revoke active admission leases for those addresses. This releases model capacity; it does not replay interrupted requests or declare their tasks complete. Final stopped state releases the hold after its owning transition ends. Delete also removes the instance profile and runtime-state record after cleanup.

Failure, rollback and cancellation

flowchart TD E[Lifecycle exits unsuccessfully] --> C{Cancelled?} C -->|Yes| Q{Controller closing?} Q -->|Yes| R[Retain recovering intent] Q -->|No| X[Record cancelled without rollback] C -->|No| B{Restart rollback eligible?} B -->|Yes| S[Stop failed candidate] S --> L[Launch previous successful resolved snapshot] L --> V[Verify readiness and model bindings] V --> O{Restoration succeeds?} O -->|Yes| D[Release hold and record rolled_back] O -->|No| F[Record failure and retain hold] B -->|No| N[Record failed or blocked] N --> U[Release eligible new holds] X --> U

Rollback is eligible for a restart that changed the launch and has a prior snapshot. It uses the retained successful launch snapshot and its requested input, without recomputing recommendations. It leaves the user's saved candidate edits intact. The prior error remains visible even when restoration succeeds. Failed cleanup or restoration retains ownership for repair. An error while stopping, relaunching or verifying the restored instance follows the restoration-failure branch. A timeout before launch changes is recorded as blocked; other failures are recorded as failed. Explicit cancellation never starts rollback that could race a later Stop.

The final cleanup rule releases a newly acquired hold only if the operation never changed the launch, ended blocked/failed/cancelled and has no active successor. Previously held endpoints remain with their existing owner. These distinctions prevent a failed replacement or an incomplete stop from looking ready for traffic.

Controller startup and recovery

sequenceDiagram participant C as Controller lifecycle participant M as Inference manager participant S as Native receipt store participant P as Portal records and service C->>M: Start management with recovery optionally deferred M->>P: Read nonterminal operations and retained holds loop Each unfinished operation opt Originating native run is available M->>S: Read originating invocation receipt end alt Awaiting receipt without accepted result M->>P: Mark interrupted without replay else Accepted receipt or later operation state M->>P: Mark queued for recovery end end M->>P: Start Portal without independent instance restoration alt Portal starts successfully P-->>M: Management started M->>M: Publish launch and binding observations C->>M: Release deferred recovery when Controller is ready M->>M: Launch recovered operations once M->>P: Enqueue desired-running instances without another recovery owner else Portal startup fails P-->>M: Startup error M->>P: Record management failure and block pending operations end

The receipt gate accepts recovered native results with status success or completed. A failed Portal startup marks pending operations blocked and publishes a management error; the later successful steps in the diagram do not run. A recovered subsystem-wide operation owns restoration for all instances. Otherwise, unowned desired-running instances restart from their last successful requested configuration. Orphan holds without a recovering operation owner are retired.

Inference subsystem restart and shutdown

sequenceDiagram participant M as Lifecycle manager participant P as Portal coordinator participant S as Supervisor participant R as Native admission M->>M: Snapshot desired-running requested configurations M->>P: Drain with restart intent only for subsystem restart P-->>M: Owned worker cleanup completed M->>R: Release active model calls on held endpoints M->>P: Cancel and join remaining Portal tasks M->>S: Close supervisor M->>P: Close management HTTP client alt Subsystem start or restart M->>P: Start management without automatic restoration M->>P: Restore captured desired-running instances M->>M: Rotate boot identity and publish ready management M->>P: Verify instance readiness and model bindings else Subsystem shutdown M->>M: Publish stopped management end

This is separate from shutting down the whole Controller. InferenceManager.close stops observers, cancels and joins lifecycle tasks, then drains Portal while preserving restart intent. It marks itself closed only after cleanup succeeds. A cleanup exception leaves the manager open for the Controller's retained-owner retry path. Management readiness and individual engine readiness are separate states.

Binding a model role

Main, Helper and Vision connections use the shared model-routing authority. An accepted task retains a versioned binding identity, while settings can select a new binding for later work. Historical credentials remain in the private store for those accepted tasks.

sequenceDiagram participant U as User or authorized tool participant M as Inference manager participant P as Ready model endpoint participant S as Private store and binding history participant R as Model-routing authority U->>M: Bind one role with current routing revision M->>R: Check expected revision M->>P: Verify served model inventory P-->>M: Compatible explicit model or valid auto selection M->>S: Save new private credential identity and binding version M->>R: Bind selected role with revision checked again R-->>M: Updated routing configuration M->>S: Save current role binding M->>M: Publish detached current and historical bindings M-->>U: Updated role without exposing private key

The Portal secret/version writes and routing update are separate operations. A revision conflict after verification can leave an unused credential/version record; it does not authorize overwriting the new routing choice. Editing one role does not reapply another role. Detaching clears managed identities while retaining the role's endpoint, model and credential in routing settings. If Controller prompt caching is enabled, binding may also prepare supported flags in the saved launch profile; it does not restart the engine to apply them.

Resolving a managed client at dispatch

sequenceDiagram participant A as Native admission owner participant M as Inference manager participant C as Captured model client participant D as Discovery and wire caches A->>M: Resolve client from published launch and binding memory M->>M: Require ready generation and matching accepted binding alt Launch generation changed M->>D: Invalidate previous endpoint and model evidence M->>C: Install current endpoint and pinned binding credential M->>C: Clear wire and context measurements M->>C: Install generation-scoped thinking capability opt Metadata refresh requested M->>C: Prepare model metadata end M->>C: Record resolved launch generation else Same generation M-->>A: Reuse resolved generation end M-->>A: Resolved generation or readiness error

Dispatch reads published memory rather than querying Portal SQLite. Metadata discovery uses the same admission fence as model generation. If resolution changes the endpoint identity after taking a lease, the metadata gate releases that lease and retries admission for the new endpoint. Generation changes invalidate old wire, context-measurement and thinking-preservation evidence. A stopped or missing managed instance fails readiness; it does not silently select an external provider.

Verification scope

Controller inference fixtures exercise shared guards, deferred receipts, idempotency, admission holds, force-stop, rollback, recovery and versioned connections with temporary state and mocked worker actions. The native receipt-ordering fixture uses a scripted model and checks the stored invocation before releasing the lifecycle intent. These checks establish control ordering, not live GPU capacity or backend compatibility.
